title: Catalysts
examples: What is the difference between a catalyst and a reactant?
Can a catalyst be used in different types of reactions?
Do catalysts change the amount of product made?

explain.say: A catalyst speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up itself.
This new path is called an alternative pathway for the reaction.
Enzymes are biological catalysts found inside living things like us.
When a catalyst is mixed with reactants, it can work in different ways.
For example, platinum metal can speed up reactions happening in a gas.
In real life, car exhaust pipes use catalysts to clean harmful gases.

faq.q: Does a catalyst change the overall energy of the reaction?
faq.a: No, a catalyst only changes the path the reaction takes. It does not change the energy difference between the starting materials and the final products.
asks: Does it change the total energy?

faq.a: No, catalysts can be metals, biological molecules like enzymes, or even acids. They just need to speed up a reaction.
asks: Must the catalyst be a metal?

faq.q: Why are enzymes so important in the body?
faq.a: Enzymes speed up the thousands of chemical reactions needed for life processes. Without them, life would happen too slowly to sustain us.
asks: What do enzymes do for us?
How fast do enzymes make things happen?

faq.q: What is the difference between heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysts?
faq.a: Heterogeneous means the catalyst is in a different state, like a solid in a liquid. Homogeneous means the catalyst is in the same state as the reactants.

faq.q: Can a catalyst be used repeatedly?
faq.a: Yes, that is one of their most useful properties. They speed up the reaction and are then free to speed up another one.
asks: Is it consumed in the reaction?

facts: A catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction.
It works by providing an alternative reaction pathway.
Enzymes are proteins that act as biological catalysts.
Heterogeneous catalysts are in a different phase than reactants.

quiz.show: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up is called a:

wrong.0: Activation energy is the minimum energy needed to start a reaction, not the substance itself.
wrong.2: Reactants are the substances that are used up during the chemical reaction.
wrong.3: Products are the substances formed at the end of the chemical reaction.

quiz.say: When an enzyme works, it binds to a specific molecule at its:

quiz.why: The active site is the specific spot on the enzyme where the reactant, or substrate, must attach to start the chemical change.

quiz.say: If a solid catalyst is used in a liquid mixture, this is classified as:
quiz.show: Solid catalyst in liquid mixture is:
quiz.why: Because the catalyst (solid) and the reactants (liquid) are in two different physical states, it is heterogeneous.

wrong.0: Homogeneous means the catalyst and reactants are in the same state, like both being dissolved in the liquid.
wrong.1: This only describes the source (like an enzyme), not the physical state difference.
wrong.2: Reversible describes if the reaction can go backward, not the physical mixture type.
